## Function Parse Command

argv into one Command or a usage error.

Behaviour: parseCommand(argv) scans argv left to right. A token starting with "--" is a flag: --pretty, --judge, --write, --md, --commit take no value; --root, --deck, --processor, --run-id, --deadline, --max-cards, --max-retry-batches, --slice-cap-bytes, --spec, --component, --map, --out, --checks, --batch, --issue, --seed-file, --from-scout, --scout, --mutants, --mutant-timeout, --test, --id, --model, --from-run, --pick, --name, --language, --module, --templates, --only, --stubs, --refs take the next token whatever it is; another flag (--x=y too) → "unknown flag: <t>"; a value flag last → "flag <t> needs a value"; a flag twice → "flag <t> given twice", but --component repeats, values in argv order (the first error by argv wins). Other tokens are words naming the command: none → "no command (commands: deck check, plan, run, submit, collect, primer, scout, review, card, accept, init)"; run; plan ("plan --from-scout" with --from-scout); submit; collect; primer; scout; review + two words <base> <head>; card; accept; init; gate; deck check; a first word report → NotYetError "command report is not available yet"; deck add|status|reset|clear → NotYetError "command deck <w> is not available yet"; else "unknown command: <words, space-joined>". An extra word → "unexpected argument: <first extra>". Then in order: a flag the command does not take → "flag <f> does not apply to <command>", in argv order (all take --root, --pretty; deck check --deck, --slice-cap-bytes; run --deck, --processor, --run-id, --deadline, --max-cards, --max-retry-batches; plan --spec, --component, --map, --judge, --out, --checks, --only; review --spec, --map, --scout, --mutants, --mutant-timeout, --test, --write; submit --deck, --processor; collect --batch; primer --write; scout --processor, --issue, --seed-file, --deadline; plan --from-scout --from-scout, --out; card --deck, --id, --md; accept --deck, --id, --model, --commit, --from-run, --pick; init --name, --language, --module, --templates; gate --deck, --stubs, --refs, --mutants). Below I = ^[A-Za-z0-9._-]+$, and "<f> ~ P" = a value not matching P → "<f> must match P (got '<v>')", P written out. card and accept: no --deck → "missing --deck", no --id → "missing --id", --id ~ I (accept: an --id holding "," must be distinct ids joined by ",", each matching I, else "--id must be distinct card ids joined by \",\" (got '<v>')"); a --pick not distinct names joined by ",", each matching I → "--pick must be distinct answer names joined by \",\" (got '<v>')"; else done (model null with --from-run; fromRun, then pick (names in order), each key only when given). init: no --name → "missing --name", --name ~ I, no --language → "missing --language", not typescript, python or go → "--language must be one of typescript, python, go (got '<v>')", --module ~ ^[A-Za-z0-9._/-]+$, else done (module, templates null when not given). review: fewer than two refs → "review needs two refs: <base> <head>", --scout ~ I, --mutants then --mutant-timeout not a positive integer, else done (mutants null, mutantTimeoutSeconds 120, test null when not given). plan --from-scout: --from-scout ~ I, else done (out null when not given). plan: no --spec → "missing --spec"; ## Function Run Tool

One READ, GREP or LIST executed over the listing through the cage and the injected file system, its text capped in lines and characters; LIST shows each file's line count.

Behaviour: runTool(action, tree, fs, caps {readLines, readChars?, grepHits, grepLineChars, listEntries, grepSkip: string[] (path prefixes)}) → {text, read: action is a READ, error: string | null}. DEFAULT_TOOL_CAPS = {readLines 400, readChars 12000, grepHits 200, grepLineChars 300, listEntries 300, grepSkip [".morph", "decks"]}. A failure: error = its message, text = "<READ|GREP|LIST> failed: <error>"; else error null and text = its lines "
"-joined, no final newline. A file's lines: its text split on "
", one trailing "" removed from each, the last piece dropped when it is "". The listing is walked in code-unit order. READ: Cage Path (file) refused → its error; fs.readFile(posix join of root and the caged path) throws → "unreadable: <path>"; a "\0" in it → "binary file: <path>"; 0 lines → the one line "READ <path>: empty file"; from = action.from ?? 1, from > n lines → "line range <from>-<action.to ?? n> is past the end (<n> lines): <path>"; to = min(action.to ?? n, n), last = min(to, from + readLines − 1); when caps.readChars is set, the shown lines "<i>: <line i>" from `from` on are kept while the sum of their lengths, each + 1, stays ≤ readChars, at least one, and last = the last kept (a first shown line longer than readChars is its first readChars chars + "… (+<the rest's length> chars)"): "READ <path> lines <from>-<last> of <n>", then the shown lines, then when last < to "… <to − last> more lines; READ <path> <last + 1>-<to> for the next". GREP: new RegExp(pattern) (no flags) throws → "invalid pattern /<pattern>/"; Cage Path (dir) refused → its error; skip = the grepSkip entries, one with no "/" read as <entry> + "/" (a top directory), less each entry e the caged path c names (c ≠ "" and c + "/" starts with e, or e starts with c + "/"); each listed file under the caged path that starts with no skip entry: Cage Path (file) refused or readFile throws → counted refused; a "\0" → passed over silently; each line i that the pattern tests true is a match, shown while fewer than grepHits are shown as "<file>:<i>: <line>", a line longer than grepLineChars as its first grepLineChars chars + "… (+<the rest's length> chars)". Lines: "GREP /<pattern>/ in <'the tree' or the caged path + '/'>: <m> match|matches in <f> file|files" (f = files with a match), the shown matches, "… <m − shown> more matches" when any left, "(<r> file|files refused by the cage)" when r > 0. LIST: Cage Path (dir) refused → its error; entries = the next segment of each listed file under the caged path: a file name, or a directory name + "/" with the count of its files; entries in code-unit order: "LIST <'.' or the caged path + '/'>: <k> entry|entries", the first listEntries as "<dir>/ (<c> file|files)" or, for a file, "<name> (<n> line|lines)" with n its lines read through Cage Path (file) and fs.readFile of its listed path, "<name> (binary)" for a "\0", the name alone when refused or unreadable; "… <k − listEntries> more entries" when more. LIST and GREP never read a directory; LIST reads only the files it shows.

node:path is its only Node module; its shell lines are text (P8). contour reads no file, no clock and no environment: it parses the text it is given; the package yaml is imported in Parse Document alone (P9). planner reads no file, no clock and no environment: the cli reads the record and the map and passes which files exist as a function; node:path is its only Node module (P10a). builder reads no file, no clock and no environment: the caller passes the checks, the cards, the profile and the texts of the guard, the locator and the probes; node:path is its only Node module (P10b). primer reads files and spawns git (git's gitOk, the environment a parameter) only in Primer Command, the clock only there through deps.now; Read Runs, Read Story and Render Primer are pure functions of what they are given, no network anywhere (P12a). scout reads no clock, no environment and no network and spawns nothing: Parse Turn, Spend Budget and Seed From Ownership are pure; Cage Path and Run Tool reach the file system only through the ScoutFs parameter (realpath, readFile); elapsed time is a parameter; node:path is its only Node module (P13a). scout-session reaches the model only through the processor's Send Generation and the clock only through deps.now; Run Scout reads the tree through the ScoutFs parameter; Scout Command and Plan From Scout are the scout layer's two node:fs files (git through gitOk and runGit, node:crypto for the sha256 in Scout Command), the environment a parameter (P13b). reviewer's checks (Find Obligations, Check Envelope, Check Guardrails, Plan Mutants, Render Findings) are pure functions of the record, git's outputs and the texts they are given: no file, no clock, no environment, no child process, no Node module (P14a). review-session spawns only through acceptance's Run Acceptance (the mutant runs, each under its timeout) and git's Run Git; - No Network In Tests: tests/setup.ts makes fetch, XMLHttpRequest, WebSocket and net.connect throw "network blocked in tests"; only the processor's own transport is mocked.
- No Shell Outside Acceptance: child processes are spawned only by Run Acceptance, the git module (in Run Git alone, P6) and the processor's none; everything else is pure.
